questions.question_text: How is Wyoming's real estate recovery account funded?
questions.correct_answer: A $20 fee from each license issuance or renewal
distractors: A percentage of each commission earned
Annual appropriations from the general fund
A one-time $100 fee at initial licensure only
questions.explanation: Wyoming funds its recovery account through a $20 fee collected every time a person obtains or renews a real estate license. The fee is not based on commissions, general fund appropriations, or a one-time charge.

questions.question_text: The recovery account balance has reached $20,000. A licensee renews and pays the $20 fee. How is that fee allocated?
questions.correct_answer: $10 to recovery account and $10 to education fund
distractors: The entire $20 goes to the recovery account
The entire $20 goes to the education fund
Collection of the fee stops at $20,000
questions.explanation: When the recovery account balance reaches $20,000, the $20 fee is split equally: half goes to the recovery account and half to the Real Estate Education Fund. The fee does not stop being collected at that threshold.

questions.question_text: The recovery account balance has grown to $55,000 while the education fund balance is $30,000. Where do newly collected license fees go?
questions.correct_answer: All fees go to the education fund
distractors: Fees are split equally between both funds
All fees go to the recovery account
Fee collection is suspended entirely
questions.explanation: Under W.S. 33-28-201(b), once the recovery account balance reaches $50,000, all of the $20 fee is deposited in the Real Estate Education Fund; the half-and-half split applies only while the recovery balance is between $20,000 and $50,000. Collection does not stop here, because W.S. 33-28-206(a) halts collection only when the recovery fund AND the education fund each exceed $50,000 — and the education fund is only at $30,000.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of Wyoming's Real Estate Education Fund?
distractors: To reimburse consumers harmed by licensees
To pay for licensee continuing education tuition
To fund real estate scholarship grants
questions.explanation: The Real Estate Education Fund is used by the Wyoming Real Estate Commission to fund its educational programs. It is separate from the recovery account, which reimburses consumers. The fund does not pay individual licensee tuition or scholarships.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of Wyoming's Real Estate Recovery Account?
distractors: Fund continuing education for licensees
Pay for WREC office operating expenses
Provide loans to first-time homebuyers
questions.explanation: The Wyoming Real Estate Recovery Account (W.S. 33-28-201) exists to compensate persons who hold a court judgment against a licensee on the grounds of fraud, willful misrepresentation, deceit, or conversion of trust funds arising out of a transaction in which the licensee performed real estate activity (W.S. 33-28-202(a)). Ordinary negligence is not a covered ground. It is a consumer protection mechanism, separate from the Education Fund, which underwrites WREC educational programs under W.S. 33-28-206(b).

questions.question_text: What is the maximum amount a claimant can recover from Wyoming's recovery account for a single claim?
distractors: $25,000 per claim
$50,000 per claim
$15,000 per claim
questions.explanation: W.S. 33-28-202(a) caps payment from the real estate recovery account at 'not more than ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00)' per claim. Payment is further limited to the actual damages included in the judgment that remain unpaid, so punitive damages, attorney fees, and court costs are not recoverable from the account.

questions.question_text: A buyer suffers $8,000 in damages from a licensee's fraud. What must the buyer do BEFORE the recovery account will pay?
questions.correct_answer: Obtain a court judgment and attempt to collect
distractors: File a complaint directly with WREC
Submit a demand letter to the licensee's broker
Request mediation through the local board
questions.explanation: Wyoming requires a final court judgment against the licensee on a covered ground, plus a showing that collection failed — a writ of execution returned unsatisfied or insufficient property to levy on (W.S. 33-28-202(a); 33-28-203(b)(iii)). A WREC complaint alone is not sufficient. The claimant must also notify the commission in writing when the suit is filed, the suit must be commenced within one year after the cause of action accrued, and the petition for payment must be filed within one year of termination of all proceedings including appeals (W.S. 33-28-203(a); 33-28-202(a)).

questions.question_text: The recovery account pays $10,000 on a valid claim against licensee Martinez. What happens to Martinez's license?
distractors: Remains active with a public notation added
Permanently revoked with no appeal available
Placed on probation for a two-year period
questions.explanation: Under W.S. 33-28-204, when the recovery account pays a claim the commission must immediately suspend the judgment debtor's license. The licensee cannot be relicensed or reinstated until repaying the full amount paid from the account with interest of 18% per annum. A discharge in bankruptcy does not relieve the licensee of this suspension, and repayment does not bar separate discipline under W.S. 33-28-111. The license is not permanently revoked.

questions.question_text: Licensee Chen's fraud caused $15,000 in actual damages. A court awards the full amount. How much can the claimant recover from the fund?
distractors: $15,000, the full judgment amount
$7,500, which is half the judgment
$5,000, the base recovery limit
questions.explanation: Regardless of the judgment amount, W.S. 33-28-202(a) caps payment at 'not more than ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00)' per claim, and only actual damages count. The claimant must pursue other collection methods for the remaining $5,000. Note that $10,000 is a ceiling, not a guarantee: under W.S. 33-28-202(b), if the account cannot pay all valid claims on file, payments are prorated among claimants.

questions.question_text: A consumer files a claim against Wyoming's recovery account. Who bears liability if the fund has insufficient money to pay?
questions.correct_answer: The state has no liability for claims against the fund
distractors: WREC must cover the shortfall from its budget
The state general fund covers remaining amounts
The claimant can sue the state for the balance
questions.explanation: W.S. 33-28-201(c) provides that no general fund monies may be appropriated for recovery account expenses and that those expenses 'shall not be paid by the state' — the section is captioned 'no liability of state.' If the account is short, claimants cannot compel the state to make up the difference; instead W.S. 33-28-202(b) prorates the available money among all valid claims on file, without regard to the order in which judgments were obtained or claims were filed.
